targets.authors: Bokobza, L., Krishnarajan, S., Nyrup, J., Sakstrup, C. and Aaskoven, L.
targets.title: The morning after: cabinet instability and the purging of ministers after failed coup attempts in autocracies
targets.evidence_quote: We replicate the analysis provided in Bokobza et al. (2022).
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
The materials produced the exact same results as reported in the
paper and appendix. We could not detect any coding errors or other issues and the
reproduction was seamless.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
Using coup risk rather than coup attempts as main independent variable (IV)
does not significantly affect the results when using country-fixed effects. However, when
the models are estimated using leader-fixed effects, the results are no longer significant.
This invites future research to explore the differences between coup attempts and coup
risk as drivers of purges.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original numbers were exactly recovered. Although the abstract and conclusion summarize the findings as robust, the alternative coup-risk specification removes significance under leader fixed effects; additional coup-proofing controls also remove significance in the all-controls country model. These are substantive qualifications under the axis rule requiring at least one reasonable alternative, hence robustness challenges.

reasoning: Re-runs and alternative analyses of original data, with no fresh sample. One original paper covers both country- and minister-level analyses. DOI identity is corroborated by Crossref title and the supplied primary PDF.
